title: Deepfake videos - is Indian law equipped to handle them
p1:
A video can show a person saying something they never said. A voice can sound exactly like theirs. So, can we still trust what we see online?

Deepfakes are changing the way misinformation spreads, but the bigger question is whether our laws are ready for this new challenge.
p2:
Many people believe deepfake videos are a completely new legal problem. The surprising fact is that India already has laws that can apply to such cases, including rules related to identity misuse, privacy violations, fraud, and harmful online content.

However, the challenge is speed. Creating a fake video may take minutes, while proving who created it and taking legal action can take much longer.
p3:
The real issue is not only having laws, but making them work effectively in a fast-moving digital world. Awareness, quick reporting, stronger technology, and responsible use of AI will all play a role.

Before believing or sharing a viral video, checking its source may become one of the most important digital habits of the future.
conclusion: Do you think Indian law needs stronger rules specifically for deepfakes, or are existing laws enough to handle this threat?
